$comment: gzip byte ceilings for dist javascript. Ratchet down as the skeleton matures; raising a budget requires review.

notes.devkit: 5400 -> 6400 (v9.14): the paired report gains the resolution of its own deltas — pairedResolution (Wald interval on the paired difference, the smallest difference the cases could detect at 80% power, and the rule of three when two arms never disagreed) plus casesForEffect, which turns an observed discordance rate into the number of cases a 2pp claim would need. Measured 5352 -> 6281 B gzip over both module formats: about 0.9 KB for a capability the report quotes on every comparison, priced here rather than absorbed silently. The package had 48 B of headroom, so no existing export was near its ceiling and none was removed to pay for this. 6400 -> 6900 (v9.22): the pairing became one function. `pairByOccurrence` returns the aligned pairs and the two leftovers so that `compareArms` and `strata.pairCases` fold over the same alignment — the divergence between them was a real defect: the two readers of one artifact counted 2 pairs where the other counted 3 on a split that repeats a question. Measured 6387 -> 6766 B gzip over both module formats: about 0.4 KB for an exported function and two exported types, which is the price of not keeping two definitions of the same concept. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative was leaving the second definition in place.
notes.ai: 35000 -> 36000 (v9.3): the pairwise selector adds a prompt builder, a parser and a knockout loop, about 1.1 KB gzip. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift, and the two prompt builders were merged onto one rules block and one candidate renderer first, which returned 155 B. 36000 -> 39000 (v9.9): the empty-result turn adds the message builder, the blind control's text and the retry loop, plus a second exported builder so the runner continues the same conversation instead of rebuilding it — about 1.6 KB gzip over both module formats. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently. 39000 -> 41000 (v9.13): the decomposition prompt adds a rule block and a reader that takes the last block, plus one exported parser and its step counter — about 0.7 KB gzip per module format, and the ceiling moves by the smallest step that keeps a capability from being absorbed silently. 41000 -> 42000 (v9.21): the per-call meter files each call under the purpose it declared, so a multi-call arm's bill can be read as a table rather than an argument. Measured 40281 -> 41271 B gzip over both module formats: about 1.0 KB for a bucket map, its accumulator and three exported types, after the character and token loops were merged onto one write point and the internal label constant was kept out of the public surface. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; the ceiling moves by the smallest step that keeps it from being absorbed. 42000 -> 43000 (v9.24): the audit turn — one call that asks the model which of the question's conditions its own statement failed to write, and adopts the statement it writes next. It adds the message builder, the reply counter, the loop that decides whether to keep the rewrite, and a purpose label so the call is billed as its own row instead of disappearing into generation. Measured 41271 -> 42735 B gzip over both module formats: 1,464 B for the only mechanism here aimed at the 16.1-18.8pp of failures no result-based trigger can see. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; the ceiling moves by the smallest step that keeps it from being absorbed. 43000 -> 45000 (v9.25): the format contract. `replyShape` reads four dimensions off one reply that every reader in this package already depends on — whether it fenced its statement, whether it is nothing but a decorated choice, how many STEP lines it wrote, how many omissions it named — and `formatProfile` turns a sample of them into a verdict per dimension, with a floor of three replies and a nine-in-ten threshold so that one unlucky case cannot flip a strategy. The same change widens the three strict readers (`parseChoiceToken`, the STEP line, the MISSING line) to accept the decoration a model that has never been benchmarked puts around a label it was told to write; on the arms measured here that window changes at most one case in 496, and on an uncalibrated model it is the difference between an unanswered call and a wrong one. Measured 42735 -> 43997 B gzip over both module formats: 1,262 B for the only instrument in this repository that reads a reply before any result exists, and therefore the only one that can predict a backbone collapse instead of reporting it as a lower score. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently. 45000 -> 46500 (v9.26): the request contract. `turnTemperature` is three lines, but `refusalDetail` is the cost: a 4xx body is JSON in three disagreeing shapes, plain text from a proxy, or an empty page, and turning each into one sentence with a 200-character ceiling is ~25 lines in both module formats. The alternative was a provider that reports every refusal as "the endpoint is unreachable", which is the one diagnosis that sends a deployment at the network when the fault is in the request. Paid for here rather than absorbed: measured 43997 -> 45336 B gzip. 46500 -> 48500 (v9.27): the deployment-time adaptation layer. `packages/ai/src/adapt.ts` adds the four bounded strategies as a table, the three layers that choose among them (`probeProtocol` reads a refusal's status and the first reply's shape, `admissible` drops the selector when a model never writes a parseable choice, `chooseStrategy`/`createObserver` switch only when Wilson intervals separate), and `wilson` itself so that the runtime decision and the published report share one definition of "better". Measured 45336 -> 48210 B gzip over both module formats: 2,874 B for the only code in this repository that decides what to run on a model nobody has benchmarked, which the cold-start harness (eval/bird/adapt.ts) then prices at 1.1-1.6pp of regret and declines. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative was shipping a default with no way to leave it. 48500 -> 49000 (v9.28): the agreement mark. The selector was shown each candidate's statement, row count, column count and three preview rows, and never the one fact a 2+1 pool turns on — that two of the three returned exactly the same thing — because three hundred characters of a wide result cannot establish equality. The cost is one optional field on `Candidate`, a render line per agreeing candidate, a header line and one rule sentence, plus the two helpers that count distinct results: measured 48210 -> 48754 B gzip over both module formats, 544 B. The block is emitted only when a caller supplies marks, so every arm measured before this one keeps a byte-identical prompt and the ablation prices the information rather than a rewrite. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently. 49000 -> 54500 (v9.29): the capability contract. `capability.ts` declares what an endpoint does with a request (family, whether sampling is honoured, whether JSON mode is served, the answer budget, whether the prompt may ask for reasoning), derives it from the model name, and rewrites the request so that a parameter the endpoint discards is removed instead of sent and forgotten. The same change carries the declaration through `withCallCounter`, reports the removal per call and per arm, gives the selector a second instruction for a judge that thinks before it answers, and adds a reader that takes the choice from the final line only when that instruction was sent. Measured 48754 -> 52129 B gzip over both module formats: 3,375 B for the layer that makes "swap the backbone" a decision the pipeline can see, and for the two defects it exposed — a metered provider that dropped the declaration, and a retry turn that rewrote the reasoning model's statement with the chat model. The chat request is byte-identical to the one every published reading was taken with, so no existing number moves and none had to be re-measured to pay for this. 54500 -> 56000 (v9.31): choosing without a call. `chooseCandidateByRule` adds the three rules the artifacts have been priced with — first, shortest, modal — plus the result-set key those rules need and the type that names them, about 2.4 KB gzip over both module formats. Measured 52129 -> 54496 B, which left 4 B of headroom against the old ceiling: the budget is raised rather than the capability trimmed, because the rule is the cheaper side of every selection this repository has measured and a deployment that cannot pay for a fourth call has to be able to say so. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift. The key mirrors `resultKey` instead of importing it (PKG2 forbids a production package from depending on the devkit), and a test holds the two to the same answer over a table of values, so the mirror cannot become a second definition of equality. 56000 -> 57500 (v9.32): the value lookup. `buildValueGapFeedback` renders the values a column does hold where the diagnosed turn could only name the three causes, with a per-literal cap, a per-value clip and the same 900-character ceiling the repair turns live under; `emptyRetryMessages` gains the third mode and degrades to the diagnosed text when the lookup found nothing. Measured 54496 -> 55644 B gzip over both module formats: 1,148 B for the message that turns a guess into a quotation. The lookup itself is harness code and is not in this bundle. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift; no export was removed to pay for it. 57500 -> 58800 (v9.41): the null-order guard. `guardNullOrder` rewrites one statement shape — an ascending sort behind a row cap — so that the unknown values cannot win the extreme the question asked for, and it does it only where the dialect puts NULL first (ascending in SQLite and MySQL, descending in PostgreSQL), only when the sort clause carries a LIMIT, and never on an aggregate key, whose ties a constant sort prefix reorders without changing what can be NULL. Measured 57000 -> 58068 B gzip over both module formats: about 1.0 KB for a rule that wins 6 questions and loses none on BIRD's dev split at no call and no token. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative is a documented engine behaviour nobody can state in a prompt. 58800 -> 58900 (v9.42): the base-model ledger. `withCallCounter` gains `servedModels()` — the model name each answer carried, counted per answer including answers that arrived without a usage block — and every arm row publishes the cases each base served. Measured 58782 -> 58891 B gzip: 109 B for the field that decides whether two runs compared in `docs/benchmarks.md` were the same experiment. The alias `deepseek-chat` named one set of weights in June 2026 and another in November, and an artifact that records only the string it sent cannot tell the two apart; this is the smallest change that makes the question answerable, and the ceiling moves by the smallest step that keeps it from being absorbed. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift; no export was removed to pay for it, and the 18 B of headroom this package had was not enough to hold a fact the report now prints on every arm row. 58900 -> 59500 (v9.43): the decode-mode field. `LlmRequest.thinking` plus a declared `ModelCapabilities.thinkingSwitch`, the branch in `adaptRequest` that removes the field when the endpoint never declared it and counts the removal, the wire form `thinking: {type}`, and the pipeline option that has to reach five call sites including the audit turn. Measured 58891 -> 59498 B gzip: 607 B for the field that lets a deployment choose a mode by request instead of by model name, which is the difference between a mode that survives an alias re-point and one that does not. The first version of this change compiled with the audit turn silently ignoring the option, because TypeScript does not apply the excess-property check across a spread — that is D49 shape, and it is why the field is declared on `auditStatement` explicitly and held by a test that fails when any turn drops it. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift; no export was removed to pay for it. 59500 -> 63500 (v9.44): the grounding rewrite. `groundLiterals` reads a statement's comparison sites — `column = literal` and `column in (literal, ...)`, skipped through comments, quoted identifiers and literals themselves so that `"O'Brien"` is a column and `'a = b'` is a value — asks the column what it stores, and replaces the literal with the unique spelling that equals it ignoring case. Two spellings, an absent value and an unreadable column are refused and reported rather than guessed, because a rule that invents a spelling turns a statement that returns nothing into one that returns something plausible. `applyGrounding` is the same rule over a lookup the caller already holds, so the pricing harness and the pipeline cannot drift into two definitions. Measured 59498 -> 62907 B gzip over both module formats: 3,409 B for the only rewrite in this package whose edit the data proves instead of the model asserting it, priced on 1,532 dev questions at one 300 s ceiling at 22 fires, 14 wins, 0 losses (+0.91pp, p = 0.0001). Reviewed as a capability rather than drift; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative is telling the model in a second call what one query already knows. 63500 -> 65000 (v9.45): the unfounded-cap rewrite. `stripUnfoundedCap` removes a top-level `limit` that ranks nothing — no top-level `order by`, a question that names no rank, a plain positive cap with no `offset` — and the pipeline applies it to the statement about to execute, reporting the clause it removed so an artifact can tell a rule that fired from one that had nothing to do. Measured 62907 -> 64542 B gzip over both module formats: 1,635 B, of which the depth-zero clause reader was already in the bundle and is only exported now. Priced by `bench:bird:rewrite` on four Mini-Dev arms at 49 firings, 11 repairs and 0 losses (+0.20 to +0.81pp per arm), against the same edit gated on the gold at 12 repairs and 23 losses. 64542 -> 69000: the package gained the SQL-Like reader and its instruction block. It reads a statement back into the labelled steps that produced it (intent, tables, joins, filters, group, having, order, limit) so a few-shot example can carry its reasoning and a prompt can ask for the same eight labels. The mechanism is OpenSearch-SQL's, a system that reached 69.3% on BIRD without training and credits its self-taught CoT few-shot and its SQL-Like intermediate language for much of that lead; this repository had implemented only the (question, SQL) half of the shape. Measured 64,542 -> 67,784 B gzip over both module formats for a 230-line module and a 12-line rule block. The alternative was to send the steps as free text, which is the `decompose` rule this repository already priced at a loss: the format works because the labels are fixed, and fixed labels are strings, and strings are bytes. 69000 -> 70500 (v9.24): the linker can be told to read the arm's evidence line as well as the question. The switch is three lines; the doc comment that says what it is worth is not, and neither is the comment that records why the default must not move. Measured 68,753 -> 68,885 B gzip, which is 115 B of headroom on a package that gains a paragraph every round: the ceiling is raised to 1.6 KB of slack so the next round prices its own addition instead of inheriting this one's tightness.
notes.node: 17000 -> 18000 (v9.37): cancellation that reaches the server. `pg` does not cancel a statement it has already sent, so the connector's forwarded `AbortSignal` was a comment that looked like a guarantee: aborting during `select pg_sleep(1)` returned the row a second later. The fix learns each physical connection's `pg_backend_pid()` once, asks the server to `pg_cancel_backend` it on a connection of its own when the caller aborts, destroys the connection instead of recycling a half-read protocol, and maps SQLSTATE 57014 (both our cancel and the server's own `statement_timeout`) to `NL2C_E_TIMEOUT`. Measured 16726 -> 17261 B gzip over both module formats: 535 B for the only path that makes a deadline a deadline. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative is a signal that silently does nothing.
notes.core: 36000 -> 40000 (v9.38): the query-intent renderer and its expression grammar. `packages/core/src/semantic/intent.ts` turns a JSON query description into a statement — tables, join column pairs, filters as (column, op, value) triples including ranges, grain, order — with three rules that are the reason it is a compiler and not a prompt: identifiers are validated instead of quoted (a double-quoted token that names no column is read as a string literal by SQLite, so escaping fails silently on the engine this benchmark runs), literals are rendered from values, and expressions are tokenised and parsed. The parser is most of the weight: a five-level grammar (or / and / one comparison / concat and +- / */ with function calls, parentheses, searched and simple CASE) plus the sixteen-name refusal vocabulary the harness reads as data. Measured 30187 -> 39561 B gzip over both module formats: 9,374 B for the only code in this repository that can remove a class of statement defects instead of redistributing them. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative was leaving 'the model wrote it badly' as an explanation with no instrument under it. 40000 -> 42000 (v9.39): quoting, and the schema check that quoting makes mandatory. The first probe refused 10 of 40 replies and the histogram said why: `bad-identifier` cannot be answered by a bare-word lexer when the corpus spells columns `County Name` and `Charter School (Y/N)`, which is 4.6% of the columns in BIRD's own databases. Names are now checked for what cannot appear in one and quoted when a bare word would not survive, in filters, joins, group-by keys and inside expressions (where a double-quoted token is a name and a single-quoted one is a string). Quoting is what then makes the column list load-bearing — SQLite reads a double-quoted token that names no column as a string literal — so `compileIntent` takes the schema and refuses `unknown-identifier`, which is a seventeenth refusal name and one more branch on the funnel. Measured 39561 -> 41403 B gzip over both module formats: 1,842 B for the difference between a grammar that excludes a sixth of one database's vocabulary and one that does not. 42000 -> 43000 (v9.40): what the second probe's twelve refusals asked for, read one at a time. Operators are matched without case (`IS NULL` is one predicate, not a spelling), a `null` value on the nullary ones is read as a missing value, a scalar on `in` is the one-element list it means, a filter's left side may be an expression under its own key (so `HAVING count(p.Id) > 5` is expressible, which `column` could not carry — a column name may itself contain a space and a parenthesis), a select alias is a name the statement invents and is no longer looked up in the schema, and a tokenizer that used to read `f."School Name"` as a bare name plus a stray dot now reads it as one reference. Measured 41403 -> 42168 B gzip over both module formats: 765 B, and the six changes between them account for nine of the twelve refusals a 120-question probe produced — the difference between reading what a model wrote and grading its vocabulary.
notes.mcp: 7000 -> 10500: the server gained the one tool the project is named for. `ask_question` runs the question-to-SQL pipeline and returns the statement with its rows, which means `mcp` now depends on `ai` — an edge the layering rule already permits (ai depends only on core and spec) and that no package used until now, which is why a server could run SQL and could not answer a question. Measured 6,500 -> 9,518 B gzip (+3,018) over both module formats: the tree-shaken pipeline, the schema validator and the tool definition. The alternative was to put the generation in the client, and then every MCP consumer would reimplement the guard, the repair loop and the empty-result turn — four mechanisms this package would then be unable to measure. The tool is listed only when a provider is configured, so a server with no key ships the same bytes the budget was set for and answers three tools.
notes.chart: 11500 -> 17600 (v9.31): the question-aware recommender adds a cue table, an admissibility proof per mark and the IR builder that turns the winning mark into a contract-valid chart. 17600 -> 18400 (v9.32): supportOf adds the twenty-two-mark rule table the compiler and the linter now share, and the compiler loses eleven hand-written guards to it. Both are capability, not drift: enumerateCandidates read a profile alone and could suggest five of the contract series types, and no rule anywhere knew what each mark reads, so an IR with an empty encoding compiled into a plausible picture of nothing and lint called it renderable. Measured 16752 -> 17895.
